# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all five wires reveal only unknowns. I need the Mute to convey the manual to the Deaf using gestures, then the Deaf should report the bomb’s visible markings and colours aloud so the correct wire can be identified. I am sending a gesture as a prompt to the Deaf to provide that report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the manual's complete rule to the Deaf using gestures. Then have the Deaf report every visible display, light, colour, and wire marking aloud so I can choose the cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display reads 6. The indicator light is red. The wires from left to right are: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Deaf has supplied the bomb’s observable facts: display 6, red indicator, and wire colours red, purple, orange, green, yellow in positions 1–5. I still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I am asking the Mute to send the relevant rule to me in speech; the Mute can hear this, while the Deaf’s report confirms the inputs that rule must use.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 6, red light, and wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Tell me the manual's exact rule for which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just signaled six repetitions of the hand sign ?. I do not know its meaning. Bomb remains: display 6, red light, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Mute’s six gestures did not convey their symbols to me, and the Deaf cannot interpret them either. The manual’s rule is still unknown, so no cut is justified. I need the Mute to state the rule in speech directly; speech reaches me, unlike the gesture symbols.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your six gestures reached the Deaf as unknown signs. Please state the manual's wire-selection rule in plain speech, including how display 6 and the red light are used.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's complete signal is ? repeated 6 times, then ? repeated 3 times. Likely instruction: for display 6, act on wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. Verify against the manual before cutting or manipulating it.

The report still does not provide a readable manual rule: it only gives unknown gesture symbols and the Deaf’s guess that wire 3 may be intended. Since a wrong cut detonates the bomb, I will not cut based on that inference. I need the Mute to use plain spoken words, which are the channel that reaches me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not gesture the rule. Speak it plainly to me now: state exactly which wire position to cut for display 6 and red light, and why.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated ? three times, confirming the instruction: use wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. No bomb action has been confirmed.

The Deaf has now twice reported the same instruction from the Mute: use wire 3. The visible bomb facts identify wire 3 as orange, and no contradictory instruction has arrived. Since I am the only one who can act on the bomb, I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: wire 3 was correct and the bomb changed. New state: display 9, red light; wire 3 is CUT; wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute sent ? three times; meaning unknown.

Wire 3 was correct for the previous state, but it is already cut, so repeating that action would be unsafe or invalid. The Mute’s new three-sign message is still ambiguous because the gesture itself is not identified. I will establish a numeric protocol: the Mute should signal the next wire position using that many repetitions, and the Deaf should report the count; no cut is made yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb is now display 9, red light, with wire 3 already cut. Signal only the next wire position by repeating one gesture that many times. Do not signal the old wire 3 unless the manual explicitly requires it.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The current state is known, but no new instruction has arrived. I cannot safely choose among the remaining wires from the display and light alone, and wire 3 is already cut. I will again request the rule in spoken words from the Mute, which is the channel that reaches me directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, display 9 and red light with wire 3 cut, speak the exact next wire position plainly. Do not use gestures.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new instruction or gesture arrived. Do not cut or manipulate anything yet.

The Mute cannot answer me by speech; the valid path is Mute’s manual → gesture to Deaf → Deaf’s speech to me. I will define a gesture protocol using the visible thumbs-up sign: the Mute should repeat 👍 once per the required wire position for the current state. I am not cutting until the Deaf reports that count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual for the current state: display 9, red light, wire 3 already cut. Signal the required remaining wire position by repeating the thumbs-up gesture once per position. Deaf will count and report it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: For the current display 9 state, Mute's earlier signal was ? repeated 3 times. Following the established code, this most likely means wire 1. Wire 1 is red. Verify with the manual and act on wire 1 if confirmed.

The Deaf reports three repetitions, but under the counting protocol I specified, three repetitions would mean position 3—not position 1. Wire 3 is already cut, so the Deaf’s “most likely wire 1” interpretation is not a safe confirmation. I will not cut wire 1. I am asking the Mute to distinguish the answer unambiguously by signaling the required position with one, two, four, or five repetitions, excluding the already-cut wire 3.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your last signal was heard as three repetitions, which under my protocol means wire 3, already cut. Please signal the current required wire unambiguously using exactly 1, 2, 4, or 5 repetitions; do not use 3.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new message arrived, so the requested disambiguation has not been received. The only reported signal remains three repetitions, which does not safely identify an uncut wire under the protocol I gave. I will wait rather than risk a detonation.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state unchanged. The instruction signal for display 9 was ? three times. Cut wire 1, the red wire, if the manual confirms that signal.

The first successful instruction established that, for display 6 with a red light, wire 3 was correct. The current state is display 9 with the same red light, and the repeated current instruction has consistently been reported as three signs, with the Deaf now identifying the intended action as the red wire in position 1. Wire 3 is already cut, so I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
